# The Paving List

Marta had been caretaker at Hollowbrook Primary for twenty-three years, and she knew the rhythms of the place the way she knew her own heartbeat. She knew which radiators clanked, which door hinges needed oil, and which cracks in the yard were widening year by year. So when the notice came through—the council had approved resurfacing the entire east side of the grounds, turning the scruffy patch of grass and dirt behind the kitchens into a proper parking and delivery area—she wasn't surprised. She'd submitted the request herself, three years running.

The delivery drivers had been parking on the street, blocking the crossing guard's sightlines. Parents with pushchairs couldn't get through on wet days. Last spring, a food delivery van had sunk axle-deep in the mud, and Marta had spent an afternoon laying planks like a foreman on some miserable railway project. The school needed that paving. She'd argued for it in meetings, and she'd felt a small, righteous satisfaction when the approval letter arrived.

Then she found the first seedling.
